content: The classification and monitoring of Chronic Kidney Disease (CKD) are determined by the American Diabetes Association (ADA) using three key factors: the underlying cause of CKD (C), the glomerular filtration rate (GFR) category (G), and the albuminuria category (A). The stages of CKD are categorized from G1 to G5 based on the level of GFR, with G1 indicating normal or high kidney function and G5 representing kidney failure. Albuminuria is classified into three levels: A1 (normal to mildly increased), A2 (moderately increased), and A3 (severely increased), based on the amount of albumin excreted in the urine. This classification system provides a structured framework to guide the frequency of treatment interventions and the intensity of monitoring required for patients with CKD.
